messages.content:
Based on all the research conducted, create a comprehensive, well-structured answer to the overall research brief:
<Research Brief>
How, based **only on evidence returned by the benchmark tools** and current **as of October 1, 2026**, does the public reporting associated with the **Pandora Papers** describe and connect **King Abdullah II of Jordan’s alleged offshore property network**, including: (1) identified or alleged shell companies and other entities; (2) the people connected to those entities, including advisers, intermediaries, directors, beneficial owners, and representatives where supported; (3) the relevant jurisdictions and their roles; (4) luxury residential or other real-estate properties, their locations, acquisition or ownership links, and associated entities; and (5) the documented relationships among the king, companies, advisers, jurisdictions, and properties—while distinguishing verified facts from allegations, journalistic assessments, and unresolved uncertainty, avoiding invented facts and unsupported entity IDs or relationship names, citing **only source IDs returned by the tools**, and producing a complete Markdown report followed by a fenced JSON object with exactly the arrays `findings`, `claims`, `reasoning_steps`, and `contradictions`, where each finding contains `question`, `answer`, `supporting_entities`, and `source_references`, each claim contains `claim` and `source_references`, each reasoning step contains `id`, `conclusion`, `premise_entities`, and `premise_relations`, and each contradiction contains `contradiction_id`, `description`, and `source_references`?
</Research Brief>

For more context, here is all of the messages so far. Focus on the research brief above, but consider these messages as well for more context.
<Messages>
Human: Investigate the following case using only evidence returned by the benchmark tools, then return a complete final report. Do not ask whether to continue.
Goal: Map the Pandora Papers public reporting on King Abdullah II offshore property network, connecting shell companies, advisers, jurisdictions, and luxury real-estate locations.
Target: Pandora Papers - King Abdullah II property network

Do not invent facts. Label allegations, assessments, and uncertainty. Cite only source IDs returned by tools. Include readable Markdown and a fenced JSON object containing arrays named findings, claims, reasoning_steps, and contradictions. Each finding should contain question, answer, supporting_entities, and source_references; each claim should contain claim and source_references; each reasoning step should contain id, conclusion, premise_entities, and premise_relations; each contradiction should contain contradiction_id, description, and source_references. Use IDs and relationship names only when they are supported by tool-returned evidence. Report uncertainty or omit unsupported items. The evaluator will score the report against the private benchmark annotations.
</Messages>
CRITICAL: Make sure the answer is written in the same language as the human messages!
For example, if the user's messages are in English, then MAKE SURE you write your response in English. If the user's messages are in Chinese, then MAKE SURE you write your entire response in Chinese.
This is critical. The user will only understand the answer if it is written in the same language as their input message.

Today's date is Thu Oct 1, 2026.

Here are the findings from the research that you conducted:
<Findings>
Reflection recorded: I will commission one focused research pass covering all requested dimensions: entities and alleged shell companies, people and roles, jurisdictions, properties and ownership/acquisition links, documented relationships, and careful separation of verified records from journalistic allegations or uncertainty. The final response must rely exclusively on source IDs returned by the research tool, so I will ask the researcher to quote or clearly attribute each item and avoid filling gaps from outside knowledge. After reviewing the result, I will assess whether a second targeted pass is needed, within the call budget.
**List of Queries and Tool Calls Made**

1. Search query: “Pandora Papers King Abdullah II Jordan offshore companies properties source documents International Consortium of Investigative Journalists Organized Crime and Corruption Reporting Project Guardian Washington Post.”
   - Returned:
     - “Pandora Papers: The royal ‘you know who’ from Jordan” — source identifier SRC-001.
     - “King of Jordan hidden property empire worth more than $100m, Pandora papers reveal” — source identifier SRC-002.
     - “Investigation reveals offshore assets of heads of state” — source identifier SRC-003.
     - “While foreign aid poured in, Jordan's King Abdullah funnelled $100 million into luxury homes” — source identifier SRC-004.

2. Search queries:
   - “site:icij.org/investigations/pandora-papers Jordan Abdullah companies names R Holdings V Ltd property Malibu Washington London adviser lawyer”
   - “King Abdullah Pandora Papers 36 companies names offshore adviser intermediary director beneficial owner”
   - “Guardian Pandora papers Abdullah company names trusts property dates Ascot Malibu Washington”
   - “King Abdullah Pandora Papers underlying records companies names British Virgin Islands R Holdings Panama Papers documents”
   - “Pandora Papers Jordan king offshore entities DLA Piper adviser trust company names”
   - “BBC Pandora Papers King Abdullah properties Malibu Ascot London Washington names companies 2021”
   - “King Abdullah offshore property Pandora Papers three Malibu mansions 14 properties dates 2003 2017”
   - “Pandora Papers King Abdullah lawyers DLA Piper Royal Hashemite Court properties”

3. Tool observation:
   - The returned search material repeated the same four source records.
   - The page returned under the International Consortium of Investigative Journalists URL was text headed and presented as an Al Jazeera article. The evidence below therefore attributes statements to the text actually returned by the tool, while separately recording the URL supplied by the tool.
   - No returned source supplied the names or registration identifiers of the 36 companies, the names of the three Malibu companies, the names of any trust, foundation, holding company, adviser, intermediary, director, agent, or beneficial-owner record, or exact property acquisition dates.

---

**Fully Comprehensive Findings**

## Scope and evidentiary limitations

The Pandora Papers were described as a leak of 11.9 million documents from 14 offshore service providers. The Guardian described the files as “the largest ever trove of leaked offshore data,” consisting of 11.9 million files totaling 2.94 terabytes. The files were shared by the International Consortium of Investigative Journalists with journalists in 117 countries, including the Guardian, the British Broadcasting Corporation, the Washington Post, Le Monde, El País, Süddeutsche Zeitung, Public Broadcasting Service Frontline, and the Australian Broadcasting Corporation. The source of the leaked documents was not identified by the International Consortium of Investigative Journalists. [2]

The Al Jazeera text returned by the tool stated that the investigation involved approximately 600 journalists and was based on 11.9 million documents from 14 global financial services companies. It stated that the records dated back to the 1970s, although most files covered 1996 to 2020. The investigation involved service providers doing business in 38 jurisdictions. [3]

The returned sources do not provide a complete underlying-record inventory for the Jordan-related entities. They report a total of 36 front companies, but do not name those companies or provide their registration numbers, incorporation dates, directors, shareholders, agents, advisers, intermediaries, trust companies, trusts, foundations, holding companies, or account numbers. Accordingly, no entity name or identifier beyond the descriptions below can be established from the returned sources.

## King Abdullah II

King Abdullah II of Jordan was identified in the returned reporting as a person appearing in the Pandora Papers. The reporting characterized him as having used offshore accounts or offshore companies to acquire properties in the United States and the United Kingdom. [1] [2] [3]

The German broadcaster Deutsche Welle reported that the 59-year-old monarch “used money from his various offshore accounts to buy properties in the years 2003 to 2017.” It said he was reported to have purchased 14 houses and flats in the United States and the United Kingdom for more than 91 million euros, or 106 million United States dollars, through 36 front companies registered in tax havens. [1]

Trust-firm sources quoted in the Deutsche Welle report generally referred to him as the “final beneficiary” living in Jordan, or “You know who” from Jordan. This is journalistic reporting of how trust-firm sources referred to the person; the returned material does not provide the names of those trust-firm sources, the relevant trust or service provider, or a documentary beneficial-owner entry with an entity identifier. [1]

The Guardian reported that the documents showed Abdullah had spent decades amassing an international luxury property empire worth well in excess of 100 million United States dollars. It stated that he had disguised his ownership through a series of offshore companies incorporated in the British Virgin Islands, according to records shared by the International Consortium of Investigative Journalists with the Guardian, the British Broadcasting Corporation, and other media outlets. [2]

The Al Jazeera text stated that the documents showed King Abdullah II had created a network of offshore companies and tax havens to amass a property empire worth approximately 100 million United States dollars extending from Malibu, California, to Washington, District of Columbia, and London. [3]

These descriptions are not identical in amount or formulation:
- The Guardian said the empire was worth “well in excess of $100m.” [2]
- The Al Jazeera text said it was a “$100m property empire.” [3]
- Deutsche Welle reported purchases totaling more than 91 million euros, or 106 million United States dollars, for 14 houses and flats. [1]

The returned sources do not establish whether these figures use the same valuation method, whether they refer to the same set of properties, or whether the difference is due to rounding, currency conversion, later valuation, or different inclusions.

## Entities

### Forty-six? No: 36 front companies

Deutsche Welle reported that King Abdullah II allegedly purchased 14 houses and flats through “his 36 front companies” registered in tax havens. [1]

The returned Al Jazeera text described three Malibu beachfront mansions as having been purchased through “three offshore companies” for 68 million United States dollars. [3]

The Guardian reported a “series of offshore companies incorporated in the British Virgin Islands” through which Abdullah’s ownership was disguised. [2]

The sources do not establish:
- The names of any of the 36 companies.
- Whether the three companies used for the Malibu properties are included in the reported total of 36.
- The legal form of any company.
- Whether any entity was a shell company, front company, holding company, or another form of company as a matter of registry classification.
- The incorporation dates or registration numbers.
- The directors, shareholders, agents, representatives, advisers, intermediaries, or lawyers of any company, other than the separately reported law firm DLA Piper as representing the monarch.
- The ownership percentages.
- The precise relationship between each company and each property.
- Whether the companies held assets other than real estate.

The terms “front companies,” “offshore companies,” “network of offshore companies,” and “series of offshore firms” are journalistic descriptions in the returned reporting. The sources do not provide the underlying registry records themselves in the returned excerpts. [1] [2] [3]

### Trusts, foundations, and holding companies

The returned sources do not identify by name any trust, foundation, holding company, partnership, or other specific legal entity connected to King Abdullah II’s alleged property network.

The Guardian explained generally that offshore service providers establish companies or trusts in lightly regulated jurisdictions, including the British Virgin Islands, Panama, the Cook Islands, and the United States state of South Dakota. It stated that companies registered offshore can hold assets such as property, aircraft, yachts, and investments in stocks and shares, and that holding assets in an offshore company can conceal the identity of the person to whom the asset actually belongs, or the “beneficial owner.” This is general background about offshore structures and is not a documentary identification of a particular trust or company in the Jordan-related records. [2]

Deutsche Welle’s reference to “trust firm sources” and to King Abdullah as the “final beneficiary” indicates that trust-service-provider material was reportedly used in the investigation, but the returned source does not identify a trust, trust deed, trustee, protector, settlor, beneficiary record, or trust company. [1]

### Offshore accounts

Deutsche Welle reported that King Abdullah used money from “his various offshore accounts” to buy properties between 2003 and 2017. [1]

The returned sources do not identify:
- Any bank.
- Any account number.
- Any account jurisdiction.
- Any account holder name other than the journalistic attribution to King Abdullah.
- Any account balance.
- Any payment instruction.
- Any source of funds beyond the competing characterization of personal wealth versus the allegation or implication of concealed wealth.

## Persons and roles

### King Abdullah II

- Person: King Abdullah II of Jordan.
- Reported roles:
  - Reported purchaser or owner of the properties. [1] [2] [3]
  - Reported “final beneficiary” in trust-firm references. [1]
  - Person allegedly connected to 36 front companies and a network of offshore companies. [1] [2] [3]
  - Person represented by DLA Piper. [3]
- Evidentiary status:
  - The reporting attributes the offshore and property relationships to documents in the Pandora Papers.
  - The sources also report denials by the king, his lawyers, the Royal Hashemite Court, and DLA Piper.
  - No returned source provides a named registry entry or complete documentary chain linking every reported company to the king.

### DLA Piper

- Person or entity: DLA Piper, a law firm.
- Role: Lawyer and representative of King Abdullah II.
- The returned Al Jazeera text quoted DLA Piper as saying: “Any implication that there is something improper about ownership of property through companies in offshore jurisdictions is categorically denied.” [3]
- It also quoted the firm as saying that Abdullah “has not at any point misused public monies or made any use whatsoever of the proceeds of aid or assistance intended for public use.” [3]
- DLA Piper was not identified as a director, shareholder, beneficial owner, agent, trust company, intermediary, or adviser to any named offshore company in the returned sources.

### King Abdullah II’s unnamed lawyers

Deutsche Welle reported that an immediate statement by the king’s lawyers rejected the claim that King Abdullah had used money that was not his own. The quoted statement said:

> “HM [His Majesty] has not at any point misused public monies or made any use whatsoever of the proceeds of aid or assistance intended for public use … HM cares deeply for Jordan and its people and acts with integrity and in the best interests of his country and its citizens at all times.” [1]

The returned sources do not name the lawyers in the Deutsche Welle report. The Al Jazeera text separately identifies DLA Piper as the law firm representing the monarch. [1] [3]

### The Royal Hashemite Court

- Entity: The Royal Hashemite Court.
- Role: Issuer of a public statement and representative institutional voice for the monarch.
- The Royal Hashemite Court confirmed that the monarch owned properties abroad for diplomatic visits and consultations. It said that, for security reasons, it had been important to keep the details secret. [1]
- It also stated that none of the purchases were funded by the state treasury or by foreign grants or loans received by Jordan as foreign assistance. [1]
- The Al Jazeera text reported the palace statement that the properties were “no secret,” that privacy and security reasons explained why they had not been disclosed, and that the arrangement was “not unusual nor improper.” [3]
- The palace stated that the properties and related expenditures were personally funded by His Majesty and that none of the expenses were funded by the state budget or treasury. [3]
- The palace said the properties were used during official visits and that some were used during private visits. [3]
- The Royal Hashemite Court was not identified as an owner, shareholder, director, trustee, agent, intermediary, or legal representative of any offshore company.

### Trust-firm sources

- Persons: Unnamed trust-firm sources.
- Role: Sources quoted in Deutsche Welle’s reporting.
- Reported connection: They generally referred to King Abdullah as the “final beneficiary” living in Jordan, or “You know who” from Jordan. [1]
- The returned material does not identify the trust firm, the underlying entity, the type of trust, or the persons’ names or professional roles.

### Moayyad al-Majali

- Person: Moayyad al-Majali.
- Role: Lawyer.
- The Guardian reported that Jordanian security forces detained him in October 2019, confiscated his laptop and phones, and accused him of slandering the country’s ruler after he asked how much land the king owned. [2]
- The returned sources do not identify al-Majali as an adviser, intermediary, director, beneficial owner, shareholder, agent, lawyer, or representative of any offshore entity in the Pandora Papers. His connection in the returned reporting is to the domestic public controversy over the king’s land ownership, not to the documented offshore network.

### Queen Rania

- Person: Queen Rania, King Abdullah II’s wife.
- The Deutsche Welle article described her as the king’s “Kuwaiti-born Palestinian wife” and said that Abdullah and Rania were generally seen as the modern couple of the Middle East. [1]
- The returned sources do not identify Queen Rania as an owner, beneficial owner, shareholder, director, agent, adviser, intermediary, lawyer, or representative of any entity or property in the alleged offshore network.
- No returned source establishes that she was involved in the reported property purchases.

### Dr. Maria Josua

- Person: Dr. Maria Josua.
- Role: Middle East analyst at the Hamburg-based research institute German Institute for Global and Area Studies.
- She said that it had always been clear that the royal family was wealthy and owned properties abroad. [1]
- She said the disguised real-estate purchases might have been legal, as claimed by the Royal Hashemite Court. [1]
- She is not identified as connected to any offshore company, property, or transaction.

### Karim Merhej

- Person: Karim Merhej.
- Role: Non-resident fellow at the Tahrir Institute for Middle East Policy.
- He said there was significant discontent toward the monarch and that the revelations were vindicating what many Jordanians felt about the monarch. [1]
- He also said Jordan ranked very high on the Open Budget Survey and that the Jordanian government had made its finances quite transparent, which he described as unsurprising because the country relied heavily on grants and loans from other countries and international organizations. [1]
- He is not identified as connected to any offshore company, property, or transaction.

### Annelle Sheline

- Person: Annelle Sheline.
- Role: Middle East scholar.
- She was quoted as saying that Jordan did not have the kind of money possessed by other Middle Eastern monarchies, such as Saudi Arabia, to allow a king to flaunt his wealth. She said that if the Jordanian monarch displayed his wealth more publicly, it would antagonize his people and upset Western donors who had given Jordan money. [3]
- She is not identified as connected to any offshore company, property, or transaction.

### Sven Giegold

- Person: Sven Giegold.
- Role: Green Party lawmaker in the European Parliament.
- He said: “The new data leak must be a wake-up call,” and that global tax evasion fuels global inequality and countermeasures should be expanded and sharpened. [3]
- He is not identified as connected to the Jordan-related entities or properties.

### Other people mentioned only for wider context

Deutsche Welle mentioned Prince Hamzah, King Abdullah’s half-brother, and Bassem Awadallah, a former chief of the Royal Hashemite Court, in connection with a purported 2021 coup and domestic political controversy. The article said that Prince Hamzah criticized the state of Jordan and alleged rampant corruption, and that Awadallah was widely disliked by many Jordanians because of perceived corruption. [1]

The returned sources do not connect Prince Hamzah or Bassem Awadallah to any company, trust, foundation, holding company, property, account, adviser role, intermediary role, directorship, beneficial ownership, shareholding, agency, legal representation, or other role in King Abdullah’s alleged offshore property network.

## Jurisdictions and the reported role of each

### Jordan

- King Abdullah was reported as living in Jordan when trust-firm sources referred to him as the “final beneficiary.” [1]
- The properties were described as belonging to the Jordanian monarch, but located outside Jordan. [1] [2] [3]
- The Royal Hashemite Court and the king’s lawyers said the properties were funded from personal wealth and not from the Jordanian state budget, treasury, foreign grants, or foreign assistance. [1] [3]
- Deutsche Welle reported that Jordan had received billions of dollars in development aid from the United States, the European Union, Germany, and other nations. It stated that United States aid in 2020 was 1.5 billion United States dollars, or 1.29 billion euros. [1]
- Deutsche Welle said that, according to current knowledge, development aid had not been funnelled to the palace. [1]
- A German government spokesperson said the Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development had no knowledge that development-cooperation funds for Jordan for which it was responsible had been made available to the Jordanian royal family. The spokesperson said the development-cooperation structure and disbursement of funds were linked to agreed progress on joint projects. [1]
- These statements concern the funding denial and the absence of known evidence of diverted development aid; they do not establish the complete source of funds for each purchase.

### British Virgin Islands

- The Guardian reported that Abdullah’s ownership was disguised through a series of offshore companies incorporated in the British Virgin Islands. [2]
- The returned Al Jazeera text said that more than two-thirds of the companies identified in the wider Pandora Papers investigation were set up in the British Virgin Islands. This wider statistic is not a finding that every Jordan-related company was incorporated there. [3]
- The British Virgin Islands’ reported role was offshore incorporation and ownership concealment or privacy, as characterized by the reporting. The returned sources do not name the Jordan-related companies or provide their registry identifiers.

### United States

- The United States was the location of reported properties in Malibu, California, and Washington, District of Columbia. [1] [2] [3]
- Deutsche Welle reported 14 houses and flats in the United States and the United Kingdom, acquired between 2003 and 2017. [1]
- The returned sources do not identify the United States state or municipal title records, property addresses, title-holding entities, or individual acquisition dates.

### United Kingdom

- The United Kingdom was the location of reported properties in Ascot and central London. [1] [2] [3]
- Deutsche Welle reported 14 houses and flats in the United States and the United Kingdom acquired between 2003 and 2017. [1]
- The returned sources do not provide exact United Kingdom addresses, title records, title-holding entities, or individual acquisition dates.

### California

- Malibu, California, was the location of three reported beachfront or clifftop mansions. [2] [3]
- The returned Al Jazeera text said the three mansions were purchased through three offshore companies for 68 million United States dollars in the years after the Arab Spring protests. [3]
- The Guardian described the most palatial property as a vast clifftop property, a “resort hotel-like mega mansion” containing 26 rooms. [2]
- The returned sources do not identify the three companies or provide exact acquisition dates.

### Washington, District of Columbia

- The returned sources reported three luxury apartments in a complex in Washington, District of Columbia, with panoramic views of the Potomac River. [3]
- The Guardian’s general geographic description placed the property empire in Malibu, Washington, District of Columbia, and central London. [2]
- The returned sources do not identify the apartment complex, addresses, title-holding entities, acquisition dates, or exact documentary ownership links.

### Ascot, England

- The returned sources reported a house in Ascot, described as one of England’s most expensive towns. [3]
- The returned sources do not provide the address, acquisition date, title-holding entity, or exact documentary ownership link.

### Central London

- The returned sources reported multimillion-dollar apartments in central London. [3]
- The Guardian described the property empire as extending to central London’s most exclusive postcodes. [2]
- The returned sources do not specify the number of London apartments, their addresses, acquisition dates, title-holding entities, or exact documentary ownership links.

### Other jurisdictions listed in the wider Pandora Papers investigation

The returned Al Jazeera text said that the documents behind the wider investigation were drawn from financial services companies in the British Virgin Islands, Panama, Belize, Cyprus, the United Arab Emirates, Singapore, and Switzerland. It also said the service providers did business in 38 jurisdictions. [3]

The returned sources do not establish that any particular Jordan-related company, trust, account, property, or transaction was located in Panama, Belize, Cyprus, the United Arab Emirates, Singapore, Switzerland, the Cook Islands, or the United States state of South Dakota. The Guardian mentioned the Cook Islands and South Dakota as examples of lightly regulated offshore jurisdictions in its general explanation of offshore finance, not as identified jurisdictions for a particular Jordan-related entity. [2]

## Properties and real estate

### Three Malibu mansions

- Number: Three.
- Type: Beachfront or clifftop mansions.
- Location: Malibu, California.
- Associated ownership structure: The returned Al Jazeera text reported that they were purchased through three offshore companies. [3]
- Reported total price: 68 million United States dollars. [3]
- Timing: “In the years after” Jordanians filled the streets during the Arab Spring to protest joblessness and corruption. [3]
- Exact acquisition dates: Not returned.
- Company names or identifiers: Not returned.
- Documentary versus characterization:
  - The report attributes the purchase and price to the investigation’s documents.
  - “Mansions,” “beachfront,” and “clifftop” are descriptions in the reporting.
  - The Guardian reported that Abdullah acquired three clifftop properties on California’s Malibu coast. [2]

### Malibu mega-mansion

- Type: A vast clifftop property.
- Location: Malibu, California.
- Description: A “resort hotel-like mega mansion” containing 26 rooms. [2]
- Setting: It overlooked a stretch of coastline made famous as the location of the dramatic final scene in the original 1968 film *Planet of the Apes*. [2]
- Reported status: The Guardian described it as perhaps the most palatial and “certainly the most expensive” of the king’s purchases revealed in the Pandora Papers. [2]
- Exact price: Not supplied in the returned Guardian excerpt. The Al Jazeera text gave a combined 68 million United States dollars for the three Malibu mansions. [3]
- Exact acquisition date: Not returned.
- Associated entity: The returned Al Jazeera text said the three Malibu properties were purchased through three offshore companies, but did not name them. [3]

### Three Washington apartments

- Number: Three.
- Type: Luxury apartments in one complex.
- Location: Washington, District of Columbia.
- Description: The complex had panoramic views of the Potomac River. [3]
- Reported owner: The Al Jazeera text said Abdullah owned them. [3]
- Associated entity: No entity name or identifier was returned.
- Exact acquisition dates: Not returned.
- Exact addresses: Not returned.

### Ascot house

- Number: One.
- Type: House.
- Location: Ascot, England.
- Description: Ascot was described as one of England’s most expensive towns. [3]
- Reported owner: The Al Jazeera text said Abdullah owned the house. [3]
- Associated entity: No entity name or identifier was returned.
- Exact acquisition date: Not returned.
- Exact address: Not returned.

### Central London apartments

- Number: Not specified.
- Type: Multimillion-dollar apartments.
- Location: Central London.
- Description: The Guardian referred to central London’s “most exclusive postcodes.” [2] The Al Jazeera text described the properties as multimillion-dollar apartments in central London. [3]
- Reported owner: The reporting attributed ownership to Abdullah. [2] [3]
- Associated entities: The Guardian reported a series of offshore companies incorporated in the British Virgin Islands, but did not identify which company held which London property. [2]
- Exact acquisition dates: Not returned.
- Exact number of apartments: Not returned.
- Exact addresses: Not returned.

### Remaining properties in the reported total of 14

Deutsche Welle reported 14 houses and flats in the United States and the United Kingdom purchased between 2003 and 2017. [1]

The returned sources specifically identify:
- Three Malibu properties.
- Three Washington apartments.
- One Ascot house.
- An unspecified number of central London apartments.

The returned sources do not identify the remaining properties needed to reconcile the specific locations with the total of 14. They do not establish whether the reported “14 houses and flats” includes all three Malibu properties, all three Washington apartments, the Ascot house, and every London apartment described by the other reports, or whether the reports use different counting conventions.

## Explicit relationships among the king, entities, people, jurisdictions, and properties

The following relationships are explicitly reported or attributed in the returned sources:

1. King Abdullah II was identified as the person associated with the offshore property network. [1] [2] [3]

2. King Abdullah II was reported as the “final beneficiary” living in Jordan in references attributed to unnamed trust-firm sources. [1]

3. King Abdullah II was reported to have used money from various offshore accounts to buy properties between 2003 and 2017. [1]

4. King Abdullah II was reported to have acquired 14 houses and flats in the United States and the United Kingdom for more than 91 million euros, or 106 million United States dollars, through 36 front companies registered in tax havens. [1]

5. The Guardian reported that his ownership was disguised through a series of offshore companies incorporated in the British Virgin Islands. [2]

6. Three Malibu mansions were reported as purchased through three offshore companies for 68 million United States dollars. [3]

7. The reported property locations were Malibu, California; Washington, District of Columbia; Ascot, England; and central London. [2] [3]

8. The Royal Hashemite Court stated that the king owned properties abroad for diplomatic visits and consultations and that some were used for private visits. [1] [3]

9. The Royal Hashemite Court stated that the properties and associated expenditures were personally funded by the king and not funded by the state budget or treasury. [3]

10. The Royal Hashemite Court stated that none of the purchases were funded by the state treasury or by foreign grants or loans received by Jordan as foreign assistance. [1]

11. The king’s lawyers and DLA Piper denied that he had misused public money or used aid or assistance intended for public use. [1] [3]

12. DLA Piper was identified as the law firm representing the monarch. [3]

13. Moayyad al-Majali was identified as a lawyer who asked how much land the king owned and was subsequently detained in October 2019. The returned sources do not connect him to any offshore entity or property. [2]

14. Queen Rania was identified as the king’s wife, but no returned source connected her to any offshore entity or property. [1]

15. Jordan was the country in which the king lived and the country whose court and lawyers issued the funding, privacy, security, and legality denials. [1] [3]

16. The British Virgin Islands were reported as the incorporation jurisdiction for a series of offshore companies used to disguise ownership. [2]

17. The United States and United Kingdom were reported as the property jurisdictions. [1] [2] [3]

18. The Guardian reported that the purchases occurred as United States economic and military aid to Jordan quadrupled and Jordanian citizens faced austerity as part of an International Monetary Fund bailout for the resource-poor country. This is contextual timing and does not establish that aid funded any purchase. [2]

19. Deutsche Welle reported that, according to current knowledge, development aid had not been funnelled to the palace, and a German government spokesperson said there was no knowledge that German development-cooperation funds had been made available to the royal family. [1]

## Characterization, allegation, denial, and unresolved uncertainty

### Journalistic characterization and allegation

The Guardian characterized the reported holdings as a “hidden property empire” and said Abdullah had “disguised his ownership” through offshore companies. [2]

The Al Jazeera text characterized the structure as a “network of offshore companies and tax havens” used to amass a 100 million United States dollar property empire. [3]

Deutsche Welle said the investigation had shed light on the king’s investments abroad and that the arrangements were “probably not illegal,” while also saying they were at odds with the government’s declared principles of financial transparency. [1]

The Guardian stated that using offshore companies to acquire property is not illegal and is sometimes done to protect privacy or security. It also said that offshore secrecy can open the door to money laundering. The returned source did not report that King Abdullah had been found to have committed money laundering. [2]

The Al Jazeera text said that in most countries it is not illegal to have assets offshore or to use shell companies to do business across national borders. [3]

### Denials

King Abdullah’s lawyers denied that he had used money that was not his own and denied any misuse of public money or aid. [1]

The Royal Hashemite Court stated that:
- The properties were no secret.
- Privacy and security explained why they had not been disclosed.
- The arrangement was not unusual or improper.
- The properties and all related expenditures were personally funded by the king.
- None of the expenses were funded by the state budget or treasury.
- The properties were used for official visits and, in some cases, private visits. [3]

DLA Piper categorically denied any implication that ownership through offshore companies was improper and stated that Abdullah had not misused public money or proceeds of aid or assistance intended for public use. [3]

### Matters not established by the returned sources

The returned sources do not establish:
- The names or identifiers of the 36 front companies.
